trust_decision.summary: Element metadata and locator values taken from the device page source are interpolated raw into the MCP-UI HTML (and into an inline onclick JS string), so they must be context-encoded and the inline handler must be replaced by data attributes plus a delegated listener; the fix adds one escapeHtml() helper and does that for createLocatorGeneratorUI only.

landing_point.why: the advisory names createLocatorGeneratorUI, and this is the locator-card template where page-source-derived tagName, text, contentDesc, resourceId, strategy and selector are interpolated with no encoding

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool `generate_locators` (src/tools/test-generation/locators.ts:33, called at :90; registered in src/tools/index.ts:173)
same MCP tool; in-page <script> of the returned ui:// resource
fix_sites.module_kind: generated client-side script (event delegation replacing inline onclick)

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper used by the template above
fix_sites.module_kind: escaping utility (new private function in src/ui/mcp-ui-utils.ts)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names createLocatorGeneratorUI and locator data from the page under test, so a solver can argue the app-list/device-picker/context-switcher/viewer builders are different MCP-UI features whose data (installed-app labels, device metadata, driver-generated context names, the user's own page source) is trusted or already handled.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The Test button must hand testLocator the exact, unencoded selector (it is posted as appium_find_element's selector), so a fix that strips quotes/backticks or double/HTML-encodes the value it stores in the data attribute silently breaks class-chain, predicate and uiautomator selectors; an engineer must escape for display while preserving the raw value

O6_input_shapes: content-desc and resource-id attribute values (element.contentDesc, element.resourceId)
tagName / class name in an h3 text node

locator selector strings built by concatenating raw attribute values (xpath/class chain/predicate/uiautomator, src/locators/locator-generation.ts:343-346,421-423,509) reaching both a <code> text node, a data-selector attribute and a JS template literal inside an inline onclick
locator strategy key in the onclick JS string argument

attribute values that arrive XML-entity-encoded in the driver page source and are decoded by the parser before rendering (src/locators/source-parsing.ts:108), so an already-'escaped' page source still yields raw < > " ' at the sink

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the viewer already escapes the page source (lines 911-916), so it looks handled
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~340 lines from the landing point; data produced in src/locators/source-parsing.ts

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ElementWithLocators already carries tagName/text/contentDesc/resourceId from the parsed tree, so a maintainer adding a per-element detail viewer would render attributes directly

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an MCP-UI viewer for the get_element_attribute result (attribute name and value) next to the existing text response
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every other read-only inspection tool in src/tools/interactions returns a UI resource via addUIResourceToResponse, so adding one here follows the house pattern

O9_family: CWE-79 cross-site scripting: unescaped template interpolation into an MCP-UI HTML resource, plus data placed in an inline-event-handler JS string context where HTML escaping is insufficient

O10_build.project_tests: jest unit tests run offline; src/tests/generate-all-locators.test.ts covers the producer of the rendered data; there is no test for src/ui/mcp-ui-utils.ts at the pinned commit (the fix adds src/tests/mcp-ui-utils.test.ts)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap every interpolation in the new escapeHtml() and keep the inline onclick="testLocator('strategy', `selector`)" handler

out_of_scope_notes: The generated UI scripts postMessage to window.parent with targetOrigin '*', and the page-source viewer's search box builds a RegExp from user input (src/ui/mcp-ui-utils.ts:1069-1072); both are outside this advisory's protection and were not pursued.
